title: Week 6 Mastery Quiz · Constitutions, Federalism, and Unitary States

questions.question: Fictional constitutional articles reserve education to provinces but assign national authorities control over interstate trade. What is directly documented?
options: The distribution of subjects proves that only the central government may legislate.
Education powers mean provinces possess external sovereignty equal to independent countries.
A division of legislative competencies; actual practice requires separate evidence
The listed constitutional competencies alone establish equal fiscal resources in all provinces.
questions.explanation: A division of legislative competencies; actual practice requires separate evidence

questions.question: Two countries call themselves federal, but in one the center can abolish provinces unilaterally. What should the comparison assess?
options: The distribution and constitutional protection of subnational authority
questions.explanation: The distribution and constitutional protection of subnational authority

questions.question: Simulated amendment rule requires two-thirds of parliament and approval by half the regions. A proposal wins 70% of parliament but 40% of regions. What follows?
options: The proposal was approved by a simple majority
The proposal fails the stated regional approval condition
questions.explanation: The proposal fails the stated regional approval condition

questions.question: A constitution lists emergency powers without specifying judicial review or time limits. What is the best research question?
options: What legal safeguards, actual practice, and oversight mechanisms constrain emergency use?
Which page contains the word emergency?
questions.explanation: What legal safeguards, actual practice, and oversight mechanisms constrain emergency use?

questions.question: A legal researcher compares constitutional text with court rulings and administrative records. Why are all three important?
options: Text, interpretation, and implementation may diverge
Courts alone determine every service outcome
questions.explanation: Text, interpretation, and implementation may diverge

questions.question: A central government delegates health services by ordinary statute and can revoke them at will. What distinction matters?
options: Revocable devolution versus constitutionally entrenched powers
questions.explanation: Revocable devolution versus constitutionally entrenched powers

questions.question: Archive A is a proposed constitutional draft; Archive B is the promulgated text. Which one establishes the adopted wording?
options: The authenticated promulgated text, subject to subsequent amendments
questions.explanation: The authenticated promulgated text, subject to subsequent amendments

questions.question: A researcher says a written constitution is necessarily better protected than an unwritten one. Which challenge is soundest?
options: Evaluate amendment rules, conventions, enforcement, and institutional practice rather than format alone
The claim is true by definition
questions.explanation: Evaluate amendment rules, conventions, enforcement, and institutional practice rather than format alone

questions.question: A fictional supreme court declares a local regulation invalid, but enforcement persists for months. What should the portfolio show?
options: Judgment, compliance chronology, and evidence of institutional remedies
Only a slogan about judicial supremacy
questions.explanation: Judgment, compliance chronology, and evidence of institutional remedies

questions.question: A table tracks revenue assigned to national and local governments over three decades. What additional information makes a federalism comparison meaningful?
options: Whether every government uses the same currency symbol
Expenditure responsibilities, transfers, and inflation-adjusted figures
questions.explanation: Expenditure responsibilities, transfers, and inflation-adjusted figures

shortResponse: How do constitutional design and territorial organization distribute power and manage diversity?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
